This is a small miscellaneous feature suggestion that I would like to suggest for subverses: the optional ability for the creator mod of a subverse to switch on and force titles of submissions (specifically those article submissions) to match the actual title of the submission.

This way, should the creator/owner of a subverse wish to, there would be less of (or none) of the problems of editorialized titles as a means to gain upvotes. This sort of phenomena was and is pretty popular on the news and article based subreddits on reddit, where a user would alter the title of the submission to make it more sensational, often in a very extreme way, and it is very misleading to a large part of the population that only look at headlines (which I assume will no doubt occur here as well.)

An example of this sort of behavior is something like this:

Actual title of a story: "Security chief of Finnish software company tells John Kerry to '**** off' about Snowden"

Here is what the user would submit instead:

"Finnish security chief tells John Kerry..." (Making it look more like a diplomatic thing between nations.)

It's misleading for the purpose of making it to the front page. This is also a fairly benign example. There are much worse ones out there that far more misleading and outright indicative of propaganda.

I think it would be good if the titles could be edited by others as long as it is flagged as [TITLE EDITED]

One of the very worst things about Reddit is the brain dead titles you see repeated constantly because they click-test well in some ad firm.
